The helmet isn't at any of them.
436:
That leaves one lead:
Prokhorov, the cloakroom attendant.
437:
But we couldn't follow it up:
Prokhorov didn't come to the meeting.
438:
He must suspect something.
He's quit his job and hasn't been home.
440:
My deepest apologies, and many thanks.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home and celebrate New Year.
Thank you very much.
- What about my men?
442:
We'll take your charges back into custody
today.
443:
If the cloakroom attendant turns up,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you, but Bely,
the real Docent, escaped from prison today.
445:
Incredible but true.
It's dangerous for you to keep
looking like him.
446:
Could we wait until tomorrow?
It is New Year, and they've tried
in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city.
It's unlikely Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't take one step
off the property! Oh, we forwarded
your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply. It's addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on New Year's
Day, promise? - We promise!
451:
Such a nice woman. Shame her father's
a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all the shouting? Who let you out?
- He's back. That not-so-good person.
454:
The New Year is here.
I hope this year brings each of you
a new beginning.
455:
Anything can happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... One moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of anything he says anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of?
He said he'd find us anywhere
and cut our throats.
461:
They say he slit Freckles' throat
with a razor. Just like that.
- The jackal's gone completely savage.
462:
Who's come to visit?
Father Frost, with presents for you!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on. Wear these in good health.
Slippers for home.
464:
- What do I need them for?
I don't even have a home.
- You will. The future's ahead of you.
465:
- For now, they'll come in handy in prison.
- You always have to jinx everything.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
And this is for you, Gavrila Petrovich.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- And this is for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's no fun without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and talk,
have a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm no prosecutor. I'm not having
a heart-to-heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! You think I'm a sucker
who'd play cards with you?
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you name one starting with W:
Warsaw. Then you name one starting
with W too: Washington. Got it?
477:
Now you, Fedya.
Name one starting with N.
478:
Naryan-Mar.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Fine. Now you need one starting with R.
- Dzhambul. - Why Dzhambul?
480:
Because it's warm there.
It's my home. My mother's there.
481:
Let's try another game. I'll go out,
you hide something, and I'll come back
and find it.
482:
- Better if you found our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it while he peeks through a hole?
- No. You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch that I don't peek.
- Why me? It's always Fedya
when something needs doing.
485:
- I'll rip your trap, you little rat!
- Your trap, your trap...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mom and dad?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- He came on his own.
- So you're here too.
491:
I was going to come to your place,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry we disturbed you for nothing,
Doctor.
- That's all right.
496:
Give him valerian, some warm tea,
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It does, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, we found out
you're in prison
500:
and were very happy,
because we thought you'd died."
501:
What bastard told this little Gloom
about his father?
502:
"Mom was happy too, because
when your letter came,
she cried all day,
503:
and before that she told me
you were a test pilot."
505:
"But I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506: you're a good man, just weak-willed."
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed enough
to steal our money and blame the cabdriver.
508:
Get lost! I'll knock your block off,
you rotten radish!
510:
Shame on you! You're all forty.
Half your lives are behind you.
511:
What have you done with them?
What have you got now? What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, nothing decent or human!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we've got to get out.
That doctor will report us to the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I, you know, slit her throat
with a razor...
515: She's in the well. Go look if you like.
516: How long was my sentence? One year.
517: How much for escaping? Three years!
518:
How much for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
And for a measly fourteen years,
I'm supposed to put up with that snake?
521:
The one who put that old woman
in the well? Do what you want.
I'm going to the police.
522: Go ahead! He won't hurt you.
523:
What about you?
Will you put up with him
for the rest of your lives?
524:
Vasya, I told him earlier
I had a runny nose, and he...
525:
Enough about your runny nose.
I'm sick of hearing it. Come here.
527:
- What are you up to?
- We're cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades. The comedy's over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
Once I've served my time, that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? A watchman
at my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could shovel snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the helmet too!
What's Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are plenty of crooks,
but only one helmet.
- They'd reduce our sentences for it.
535:
Where did he put it?
We checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a runny nose,
and all you said was, "I'll rip your trap."
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When we got caught. Remember?
He said, "I'm fishing. You dive in."
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing through a hole in the ice,
540:
and you, Squint, can you swim?"
- That's it! He hid the helmet
in the ice hole!
541:
That's right! I remember, the swine!
It's in the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you jerk?
You could've left a note
before hanging yourself. - Come on.
543:
- What about him?
- Let them pick him up.
I'm not carrying that big lump. Let's go!
545:
- There's nothing in there.
- It's on the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? It's always Squint.
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- A minute ago he wanted to hang himself,
and now he's afraid of catching a cold!
- Greetings, athletes!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551:
I'd finish you off,
but I haven't got time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And there's another at the dacha.
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
